newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish budget talks break down after 14 hours.
newsitem.headline: Danish budget talks break down after 14 hours.

text.p: Negotiations between Denmark's minority government and opposition Conservatives on the 1997 state budget broke down on Friday afternoon after a marathon 14 hours of day and night talks.
"We have not been able to achieve the result we expected, we have been unable to reach agreement with the government," Conservative leader Hans Engell told journalists in parliament.
Engell said that his party would still be willing to co-operate with the government on elements of the budget on which consensus was reached.
The breakdown came despite general agreement between the sides on the goal of reducing the forecast public sector deficit of 5.8 billion Danish crowns (999 million) to zero.
Engell would give no further details of the breakdown of the talks, referring to a news conference to be held later in the afternoon.
